slot.brief: Given a standard cell potential, compute ΔG° and the equilibrium constant of the cell reaction using ΔG° = −nFE° = −RT ln K.

stem: For a cell with $n=2$, $E^\circ=0.1773$ V at $298$ K, find $(\Delta G^\circ,K)$. Take $F=96500$ C mol$^{-1}$ and $R=8.314$ J mol$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$.
working:
$\Delta G^\circ=-nFE^\circ=-2(96500)(0.1773)=-34.2$ kJ mol$^{-1}$.\n$\ln K=\dfrac{nFE^\circ}{RT}=13.81$; $K\approx9.95\times10^5\approx1.0\times10^6$.

Independent check: ΔG° = −nFE° = −2(96500)(0.1773) = −34.2 kJ mol⁻¹. ln K = nFE°/(RT) = 13.81, so K ≈ 1.0 × 10⁶.
solution:
For a cell, $4\Delta G^\circ=-nFE^\circ$ and $\ln K=\dfrac{nFE^\circ}{RT}$. 
$$\Delta G^\circ=-2(96500)(0.1773)=-34.2\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1},\qquad \ln K=\frac{2(96500)(0.1773)}{(8.314)(298)}=13.81$$
Thus $K=e^{13.81}\approx1.0\times10^6$.
